areas.limits: Pinned goldens plus seeded grammar-based exploration with bounded reduction of flags, patterns and subjects. Generated Linux x86 cases replay fully there; portable ASCII inputs replay elsewhere because upstream empty UTF matching differs by platform. Complete upstream dialect/JIT parity is not claimed.
Includes Git ignore/config, late NUL, transcoding and platform-specific contracts; exhaustive gitwildmatch/platform parity is not claimed.

areas.area: Python, Go and Rust source understanding
areas.limits: 328 upstream valid named trees; no macro expansion or semantic type resolution.
Fixture precision/recall/nDCG test plumbing and independent-line discovery, not model quality.

areas.area: Decision budgets, cache, retries and cancellation
areas.limits: Provider checks use HTTP/native fixtures. POSIX interrupt cancellation is cooperative; Windows signal behavior is not runtime-verified.
Snapshot-bound ID cursors are required. Exact scans are bounded by request/document/source/output budgets. No connector ingestion or direct remote-file downloads.
JSON events expose schema version, provenance, source revision, index time, snapshot and observation time. Local sources are live; indexed sources represent stored revisions.

Tracks startup, first stdout byte, elapsed/CPU, RSS and throughput on large files, generated small files and native Zig/Go/TypeScript repositories. VM dispatch and native CLI CPU-stack profiles guide JIT work; VM/JIT checksums must agree. Host, corpus/binary hashes and per-run results are recorded; no general ripgrep performance parity claim.

areas.status: bounded mutation and coverage fuzz campaigns
areas.limits: ReleaseSafe regex, Python/Go/Rust/JS/TS parser and dictionary targets have allocation/input/work bounds and leak checks; VM/JIT comparisons include spans, captures, marks, errors and steps. Finite campaigns are evidence, not a proof of safety for arbitrary input.
